title: Asymptotic summation in the pseudodifferential order filtration
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its positive volume form $dV$. Let $E,F,G$ be smooth finite-rank real vector bundles. Use the distribution spaces, symbol classes $S^r$ and operator classes $\Psi^r$ of [def-sfb-symbol-pseudodifferential-operators]. Let $r\in\mathbf Z$ and let $(T_j)_{j\geq0}$ be any sequence of real operators with $T_j\in\Psi^{r-j}(E,F)$. There is a single real operator $T\in\Psi^r(E,F)$ such that for every integer $L\geq1$, $$T-\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}T_j\in\Psi^{r-L}(E,F).$$ The differences are differences of continuous real-linear maps $\mathcal D\prime(E)\to\mathcal D\prime(F)$ with the distributional actions in the cited definition. No convergence of the unmodified series $\sum_jT_j$ is assumed.

source.place: Demailly, Part I §3.B, printed pp.12–14 (PDF pages 24–26); WANTED locally, read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/hodge-ams.pdf; paragraph following Definition 3.8, printed pp.13–14: the instruction to choose a symbol asymptotic to the expansion; general decreasing-order operator formulation.

proof.text: Choose the finite charts, cutoffs and compact sets of [lem-sfb-symbol-common-atlas] once for $E,F$. For a tuple of chart symbols write $Q(a)=\sum_i\chi_i\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Op}(a_i)\psi_i$. Each term is the operator of the amplitude $\chi_i(x)a_i(x,\xi)\psi_i(y)$, extended by zero: it vanishes outside the compact set $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i\times\operatorname{supp}\psi_i$, and its estimates are uniform because those of $a_i$ hold on the compact set $\operatorname{supp}\chi_i$. By [lem-sfb-compact-oscillatory-amplitude-reduction] the oscillatory limit exists on chart tests, the term and its transpose for the section–dual-density pairing are continuous, the transpose of a test is supported in $\operatorname{supp}\psi_i$, the action on all distributions is by transposition and so is continuous for the strong topologies, and the real part is the replacement $a\mapsto(a+a^\natural)/2$ on distributions. Hence $Q(a)\in\Psi^s$ by the definition when all $a_i\in S^s$. Limits of sums are sums of limits, so on tests, on transposes and therefore on all distributions $Q$ is real-linear in finite real combinations of tuples, also of different orders. Finite sums and differences in $\Psi^s$ follow directly by concatenating their defining finite representations and adding smooth kernels; $\Psi^{s-1}\subset\Psi^s$ follows from $(1+|\xi|)^{s-1-|\beta|}\leq(1+|\xi|)^{s-|\beta|}$. These observations apply to the given distributional maps.

source.place: WANTED locally. Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf; 3.5–3.6, p.7; fixed-atlas localization.

proof.text: Inductively construct tuples $a_j\in\prod_i S^{r-j}$ supported in the fixed $K_i$, and operators $R_j\in\Psi^{r-j}$, as follows. Set $R_0=0$. Given $R_j$, the sum $A_j=T_j+R_j$ is of order $r-j$ by concatenation of representations. Apply [lem-sfb-symbol-common-atlas] to $A_j$ with $s=r-j$ and define $R_{j+1}=A_j-Q(a_j)\in\Psi^{r-j-1}$. The base has order $r$ since zero has the empty representation. Summing the identities $Q(a_j)=T_j+R_j-R_{j+1}$ for $0\leq j<L$ cancels the intermediate $R_j$ and gives $$\sum_{j<L}Q(a_j)=\sum_{j<L}T_j-R_L.$$ This is an identity of maps on all distributions, and it never requires summing the remainders infinitely.

source.place: WANTED locally. Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf; 3.6–3.7, pp.7–8; agent-written order-by-order correction recurrence.

proof.text: For each of the finitely many indices $i$, apply [lem-sfb-symbol-borel-cutoff] to $(a_{j,i})_{j\geq0}$, using the common compact support $K_i$ and its global estimates supplied at every induction stage. Obtain one $b_i\in S^r$ such that $c_{L,i}=b_i-\sum_{j<L}a_{j,i}\in S^{r-L}$ for every $L\geq1$. Set $T=Q(b)$. By [lem-sfb-compact-oscillatory-amplitude-reduction] and the definition, as in step 1, $T$ is a continuous real-linear map on the strong distribution spaces, belongs to $\Psi^r$, and real-linearity of $Q$ from step 1 gives $$T-\sum_{j<L}Q(a_j)=Q(c_L)\in\Psi^{r-L}.$$ Real parts are taken only at quantization, so complex Borel symbols give real operators without any symmetry hypothesis.

source.place: WANTED locally. Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf; 3.7, pp.7–8, matrix symbol summation, followed by 3.5 and transpose action.

proof.text: For any $L\geq1$, insert the telescoping identity of step 2 into step 3: $$T-\sum_{j<L}T_j=Q(c_L)-R_L.$$ Both terms have order $r-L$; their difference has a defining representation obtained by concatenating those of the two terms and negating the second symbols and kernel. Thus it is in $\Psi^{r-L}$. The same $T$ works for every $L$. Only finitely many operator identities were used for each $L$; no convergence of $\sum_jT_j$ was asserted.

source.place: WANTED locally. Supplemental Demailly, Differential and pseudodifferential operators on manifolds, section 3, read online at https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/analytic_geometry_2019/pseudodiff.pdf; 3.7, pp.7–8; elementary assembly in the order filtration.

proof_origin.place: WANTED locally. Follows the online supplemental Demailly course, section 3.7, pp.7–8; the recurrence handles arbitrary distributional operators and their changing local representations.
